## R Markdown

## 1. Import of mouse hippocampal single-nucleus RNA-seq data

This section imports processed 10x Genomics gene-count matrices for 12 mouse hippocampal samples (WT, WT-CXCL14, AD, and AD-CXCL14; three samples per condition). Individual Seurat objects are created and assigned sample and sequencing-batch identifiers. An initial QC filter is applied before saving the per-sample Seurat object list. A second, more stringent QC step is performed in the downstream analysis. Raw and processes data are deposited on GEO GSE352519. Note: file names and sample IDs in directory may look slightly different and may have to be adjusted. 

```{r mouse-data-import}
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

sample_ids <- c(
  "109956C4", "109956C9", "109956F11", "109956F8", "109956G5", "109956G6",
  "115478C12", "115478C4", "115478E1", "115478E10", "115478E7", "139431A6"
)

# Each directory contains the processed 10x matrix files for one sample.
base_dir <- file.path("data", "CXCL14_snRNAseq")
data_dirs <- setNames(file.path(base_dir, sample_ids), sample_ids)

batch_map <- c(
  "109956C4" = "25E91", "109956C9" = "25E91",
  "109956F11" = "25E73", "109956F8" = "25E73",
  "109956G5" = "25E73", "109956G6" = "25E73",
  "115478C12" = "25E91", "115478C4" = "25E73",
  "115478E1" = "25E73", "115478E10" = "25E73",
  "115478E7" = "25E73", "139431A6" = "25E91"
)

stopifnot(setequal(sample_ids, names(batch_map)))
missing_dirs <- data_dirs[!dir.exists(data_dirs)]
if (length(missing_dirs)) {
  stop("Missing sample directories: ", paste(missing_dirs, collapse = ", "))
}

objs <- list()
for (sid in sample_ids) {
  message("Reading sample: ", sid)
  mat <- Read10X(data.dir = data_dirs[[sid]])
  sobj <- CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = mat, project = sid, min.cells = 3, min.features = 200
  )
  sobj$sample <- sid
  sobj$batch <- batch_map[[sid]]
  sobj[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(sobj, pattern = "^mt-")
  sobj[["percent.rp"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(sobj, pattern = "^Rp[sl]")
  objs[[sid]] <- sobj
}
```

```{r initial-qc}
# Summarize per-sample quality metrics before initial filtering.
qc_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(objs, function(s) {
  data.frame(
    sample = unique(s$sample),
    cells = ncol(s),
    median_nFeature = median(s$nFeature_RNA),
    median_nCount = median(s$nCount_RNA),
    median_percent_mt = median(s$percent.mt)
  )
}))
print(qc_df)

# Initial QC thresholds used to create the saved starting object.
objs <- lapply(objs, function(s) {
  subset(s, subset =
    nFeature_RNA >= 300 &
    nFeature_RNA <= 8000 &
    nCount_RNA >= 500 &
    percent.mt <= 20
  )
})

# Checkpoint loaded by the downstream analysis.
saveRDS(objs, file = "snrna_raw_objs.rds")
```



## 1. Packages and sample objects

```{r packages}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(harmony)
  library(celda)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(Matrix)
})

objs <- readRDS("snrna_raw_objs.rds")
stopifnot(is.list(objs), length(objs) == 12L, !is.null(names(objs)))
```

## 2. Stricter QC

The second QC filter retains nuclei with 300–8,000 detected genes, 500–40,000 UMIs, and ≤5% mitochondrial counts.

```{r strict-qc}
qc_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(objs), function(sid) {
  s <- objs[[sid]]
  data.frame(sample = sid, cells = ncol(s),
             median_nFeature = median(s$nFeature_RNA),
             median_nCount = median(s$nCount_RNA),
             median_percent_mt = median(s$percent.mt))
}))
print(qc_summary)

objs_v2 <- lapply(objs, function(s) {
  if (!"percent.mt" %in% colnames(s[[]])) {
    mt_pattern <- if (any(grepl("^MT-", rownames(s)))) "^MT-" else "^mt-"
    s[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(s, pattern = mt_pattern)
  }
  subset(s, subset = nFeature_RNA >= 300 & nFeature_RNA <= 8000 &
           nCount_RNA >= 500 & nCount_RNA <= 40000 & percent.mt <= 5)
})
merged_v2 <- merge(objs_v2[[1]], y = objs_v2[-1])
VlnPlot(merged_v2,
        features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA", "percent.mt"),
        group.by = "sample", ncol = 3, pt.size = 0)
```

## 3. Ambient RNA removal with decontX

Ambient RNA was estimated per sample; nuclei with contamination estimates exceeding 0.20 were removed. Original counts were retained in a separate assay.

```{r decontx}
decontx_results_v2 <- lapply(names(objs_v2), function(sid) {
  s <- objs_v2[[sid]]
  orig_counts <- GetAssayData(s, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  orig_per_cell <- Matrix::colSums(orig_counts)

  sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(s)
  sce <- celda::decontX(sce)
  decon_counts <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "decontXcounts")
  cont_vec <- setNames(as.numeric(sce$decontX_contamination), colnames(sce))
  new_per_cell <- Matrix::colSums(decon_counts)
  frac_removed <- 1 - new_per_cell / orig_per_cell[colnames(decon_counts)]

  # Keep the original SCE -> Seurat conversion method used in the analysis.
  s2 <- as.Seurat(sce, counts = "decontXcounts", data = NULL)
  s2[["RNA_raw"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = orig_counts[, colnames(s2), drop = FALSE])
  s2$decontX_contam <- cont_vec[colnames(s2)]
  s2$decontX_frac_removed <- frac_removed[colnames(s2)]
  s2$sample <- sid
  s2 <- subset(s2, subset = decontX_contam <= 0.20)

  list(seurat = s2,
       per_cell = data.frame(
         cell = colnames(s2), sample = sid,
         decontX_contam = cont_vec[colnames(s2)],
         decontX_frac_removed = frac_removed[colnames(s2)],
         orig_counts = orig_per_cell[colnames(s2)],
         new_counts = new_per_cell[colnames(s2)], row.names = NULL))
})
objs_v2_decontx <- setNames(lapply(decontx_results_v2, `[[`, "seurat"), names(objs_v2))
merged_v2_decontx <- merge(objs_v2_decontx[[1]], y = objs_v2_decontx[-1])
VlnPlot(merged_v2_decontx, features = "decontX_contam",
        group.by = "sample", pt.size = 0) +
  ylab("DecontX contamination fraction") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## 4. Doublet detection using scDblFinder

```{r doublet-removal}
doublet_results <- lapply(names(objs_v2_decontx), function(sid) {
  sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(objs_v2_decontx[[sid]])
  sce <- scDblFinder::scDblFinder(sce)
  calls <- table(sce$scDblFinder.class)
  sce <- sce[, sce$scDblFinder.class == "singlet"]
  s2 <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = SummarizedExperiment::assay(sce, "counts"), assay = "RNA")
  s2 <- AddMetaData(s2, metadata = as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sce)))
  Key(s2[["RNA"]]) <- "RNA_"
  list(seurat = s2, calls = calls)
})
names(doublet_results) <- names(objs_v2_decontx)
objs_v2_clean <- lapply(doublet_results, `[[`, "seurat")

# Counts from BEFORE singlet filtering (rather than reporting zero doublets).
dbl_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(doublet_results), function(sid) {
  tab <- doublet_results[[sid]]$calls
  data.frame(sample = sid,
             singlets = if ("singlet" %in% names(tab)) unname(tab["singlet"]) else 0,
             doublets = if ("doublet" %in% names(tab)) unname(tab["doublet"]) else 0)
}))
print(dbl_stats)
```

## 5. Combined analysis and Harmony integration

Normalization, 3,000 highly variable genes, regression of nCount_RNA, 50 PCs, Harmony on `sample` (theta = 2), and clustering at resolution 0.2 were used in the original analysis.

```{r integrated-clustering}
merged_v2_clean <- merge(
  objs_v2_clean[[1]], y = objs_v2_clean[-1], add.cell.ids = names(objs_v2_clean))
DefaultAssay(merged_v2_clean) <- "RNA"
merged_v2_clean <- NormalizeData(merged_v2_clean,
                                normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
                                scale.factor = 1e4, verbose = FALSE)
merged_v2_clean <- FindVariableFeatures(merged_v2_clean,
                                       selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 3000,
                                       verbose = FALSE)
merged_v2_clean <- ScaleData(merged_v2_clean,
                             features = VariableFeatures(merged_v2_clean),
                             vars.to.regress = "nCount_RNA", verbose = TRUE)
merged_v2_clean <- RunPCA(merged_v2_clean,
                          features = VariableFeatures(merged_v2_clean), npcs = 50)

# Original analysis used HarmonyMatrix on PCA embeddings. API is version-dependent.
pca_embeddings <- Embeddings(merged_v2_clean, reduction = "pca")
harmony_embeddings <- harmony::HarmonyMatrix(
  data_mat = pca_embeddings,
  meta_data = merged_v2_clean@meta.data,
  vars_use = "sample", do_pca = FALSE, theta = 2)
merged_v2_clean[["harmony"]] <- CreateDimReducObject(
  embeddings = harmony_embeddings, key = "harmony_",
  assay = DefaultAssay(merged_v2_clean))

merged_v2_clean <- FindNeighbors(merged_v2_clean,
                                reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20, k.param = 50)
merged_v2_clean <- FindClusters(merged_v2_clean,
                               resolution = 0.2, algorithm = 1, random.seed = 1234)
merged_v2_clean <- RunUMAP(merged_v2_clean,
                          reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20, seed.use = 1234)
DimPlot(merged_v2_clean, group.by = "seurat_clusters", label = TRUE)
FeaturePlot(merged_v2_clean, features = "Cx3cr1", reduction = "umap",
            ncol = 1, pt.size = 0.1, raster = FALSE,
            cols = c("lightgrey", "red"), min.cutoff = "q05", max.cutoff = "q95")
```

## 7. Initial microglial subclustering and contaminant exclusion

```{r microglia-initial}
microglia <- subset(merged_v2_clean, subset = celltype == "Microglia")
DefaultAssay(microglia) <- "RNA"
microglia <- NormalizeData(microglia, normalization.method = "LogNormalize", scale.factor = 1e4)
microglia <- FindVariableFeatures(microglia, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)
microglia <- ScaleData(microglia, vars.to.regress = "nCount_RNA", verbose = FALSE)
microglia <- RunPCA(microglia, npcs = 20, verbose = FALSE)

pca_embeddings <- Embeddings(microglia, "pca")[, 1:20, drop = FALSE]
harmony_embeddings <- harmony::HarmonyMatrix(
  data_mat = pca_embeddings, meta_data = microglia@meta.data,
  vars_use = "sample", do_pca = FALSE)
microglia[["harmony"]] <- CreateDimReducObject(
  embeddings = harmony_embeddings, key = "harmony_", assay = DefaultAssay(microglia))
microglia <- FindNeighbors(microglia, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20)
microglia <- FindClusters(microglia, resolution = 0.2)
microglia <- RunUMAP(microglia, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20, seed.use = 1234)
DimPlot(microglia, reduction = "umap", group.by = "seurat_clusters",
        label = TRUE, repel = TRUE, pt.size = 0.1) +
  ggtitle("Microglia Subclusters")

DotPlot(microglia, features = list(
  Homeostatic = c("Cx3cr1", "P2ry12", "Tmem119"),
  DAM = c("Trem2", "Spp1", "Itgax", "Clec7a"),
  Cycling = c("Mki67", "Top2a", "Ccnb1"),
  BAMs = c("Ms4a7", "Mrc1", "Pf4", "Lyve1"),
  Tcells = c("Cd3d", "Cd3e", "Cd8a", "Cd4"))) +
  RotatedAxis() + ggtitle("Microglia, BAM, and T cell markers by subcluster")

initial_microglia_labels <- c(
  "0" = "Homeostatic", "1" = "DAM", "2" = "BAMs", "3" = "BAMs",
  "4" = "Cycling", "5" = "Contamination", "6" = "T cells", "7" = "Contamination")
stopifnot(all(levels(microglia) %in% names(initial_microglia_labels)))
microglia <- RenameIdents(microglia, initial_microglia_labels)
microglia$subcluster_annotation <- as.character(Idents(microglia))
DimPlot(microglia, reduction = "umap", group.by = "subcluster_annotation",
        label = TRUE) + ggtitle("Microglia subclusters annotated")
```

## 8. Recluster retained microglial populations 

Homeostatic, DAM, and cycling populations were retained. BAMs, T cells, and contaminating populations were excluded prior to reclustering.

```{r microglia-recluster}
micro_sub <- subset(microglia, idents = c("Homeostatic", "DAM", "Cycling"))
print(table(Idents(micro_sub)))
micro_sub <- NormalizeData(micro_sub)
micro_sub <- FindVariableFeatures(micro_sub)
micro_sub <- ScaleData(micro_sub, vars.to.regress = "nCount_RNA")
micro_sub <- RunPCA(micro_sub, npcs = 30)
micro_sub <- RunHarmony(micro_sub, group.by.vars = "sample", dims.use = 1:20)
micro_sub <- FindNeighbors(micro_sub, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20)
micro_sub <- FindClusters(micro_sub, resolution = 0.2)
micro_sub <- RunUMAP(micro_sub, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:20)
DimPlot(micro_sub, reduction = "umap", group.by = "seurat_clusters",
        label = TRUE, repel = TRUE, pt.size = 0.1) +
  ggtitle("Microglia Harmony clusters")

# Main Figure 3B: marker expression
FeaturePlot(micro_sub,
            features = c("Tmem119", "Arhgap15", "Clec7a", "Itgax", "Mx1", "Mki67"),
            reduction = "umap", ncol = 3, pt.size = 0.1, raster = FALSE)

micro_sub <- JoinLayers(micro_sub)
markers <- FindAllMarkers(micro_sub, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25, logfc.threshold = 0.25)
top10 <- markers %>% group_by(cluster) %>% top_n(n = 10, wt = avg_log2FC)
DoHeatmap(micro_sub, features = top10$gene) + NoLegend()
```

## 9. Final microglial subtype annotations and proportions 


```{r microglia-final-labels}
final_microglia_labels <- c(
  "0" = "Homeostatic", "1" = "DAM", "2" = "Primed",
  "3" = "Cycling", "4" = "Interferon")
stopifnot(all(levels(micro_sub) %in% names(final_microglia_labels)))
micro_sub$micro_subtype <- unname(final_microglia_labels[as.character(Idents(micro_sub))])
micro_sub$micro_subtype <- factor(
  micro_sub$micro_subtype,
  levels = c("Homeostatic", "Primed", "DAM", "Interferon", "Cycling"))
Idents(micro_sub) <- "micro_subtype"
DimPlot(micro_sub, reduction = "umap", group.by = "micro_subtype",
        label = TRUE, repel = TRUE)

# Pooled cell proportions by condition, matching the original figure approach.
df_counts <- as.data.frame(table(
  Subtype = micro_sub$micro_subtype, Condition = micro_sub$Condition))
df_counts$Condition <- factor(
  df_counts$Condition, levels = c("WT", "WT-CXCL14", "AD", "AD-CXCL14"))
ggplot(df_counts, aes(x = Condition, y = Freq, fill = Subtype)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
  theme_classic() +
  ylab("Proportion of microglia") +
  ggtitle("Cell proportions per Condition by Microglia Subtype") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
```


## DAM pseudobulk differential expression, GO enrichment, and module scoring

This section uses the `micro_sub` Seurat object generated in the preceding analysis. Pseudobulk counts are aggregated by biological sample, with AD-CXCL14 compared against AD.

```{r dam-pseudobulk-setup}
library(Seurat)
library(DESeq2)
library(Matrix)
library(dplyr)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(GO.db)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# Restrict to the previously annotated disease-associated microglia (DAM).
dam_only <- subset(micro_sub, subset = micro_subtype == "DAM")

# Aggregate raw counts per biological replicate. Since each sample belongs
# to only one condition, group by sample and reconstruct condition from the
# original per-cell metadata rather than parsing Seurat column names.
pseudo_dam <- AggregateExpression(
  dam_only, assays = "RNA", return.seurat = TRUE,
  group.by = "sample"
)

# With return.seurat=TRUE, the RNA counts represent summed pseudobulk counts.
dam_counts <- GetAssayData(pseudo_dam, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")

sample_metadata <- unique(dam_only@meta.data[, c("sample", "Condition")])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sample_metadata$sample))
stopifnot(all(colnames(dam_counts) %in% sample_metadata$sample))

dam_coldata <- sample_metadata[match(colnames(dam_counts), sample_metadata$sample), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(dam_coldata) <- dam_coldata$sample
stopifnot(identical(rownames(dam_coldata), colnames(dam_counts)))

# Select the two experimental groups for this comparison.
keep_samples <- dam_coldata$Condition %in% c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
dam_counts <- dam_counts[, keep_samples, drop = FALSE]
dam_coldata <- dam_coldata[keep_samples, , drop = FALSE]
dam_coldata$Condition <- factor(dam_coldata$Condition, levels = c("AD", "AD-CXCL14"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(dam_coldata$Condition))
print(table(dam_coldata$Condition))
```

### DAM pseudobulk differential expression (original ≥200-count filter)

```{r dam-pseudobulk-de}
# Preserve the original total-count filtering and gene exclusions.
dam_counts_de <- dam_counts[rowSums(dam_counts) >= 200, , drop = FALSE]
exclude_gene <- grepl("^Gm", rownames(dam_counts_de)) |
  grepl("Rik$", rownames(dam_counts_de)) |
  grepl("^Mt-", rownames(dam_counts_de)) |
  grepl("^Rp[sl]", rownames(dam_counts_de))
dam_counts_de <- dam_counts_de[!exclude_gene, , drop = FALSE]
cat("Genes before filtering:", nrow(dam_counts), "\n")
cat("Genes retained for DE export:", nrow(dam_counts_de), "\n")

dds_dam_de <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(as.matrix(dam_counts_de)),
  colData = dam_coldata,
  design = ~ Condition
)
dds_dam_de <- DESeq(dds_dam_de)
res_dam_de <- results(dds_dam_de, contrast = c("Condition", "AD-CXCL14", "AD"))
df_dam_de <- as.data.frame(res_dam_de)
df_dam_de$gene <- rownames(df_dam_de)
head(df_dam_de)
# Optional export; uncomment after selecting an output directory.
# write.csv(df_dam_de, "DAMonly_v2_df_ADcx_AD.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### GO Biological Process GSEA (≥10-count filter)

```{r dam-go-gsea}

dam_counts_go <- dam_counts[rowSums(dam_counts) >= 10, , drop = FALSE]
dds_dam_go <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(as.matrix(dam_counts_go)),
  colData = dam_coldata,
  design = ~ Condition
)
dds_dam_go <- DESeq(dds_dam_go)
res_dam_go <- results(dds_dam_go, contrast = c("Condition", "AD-CXCL14", "AD"))
df_go <- as.data.frame(res_dam_go)
df_go$gene <- rownames(df_go)

# The original analysis used SYMBOL -> ENTREZID annotation and retained the
# first mapping per ENTREZID. Keep that behavior for comparison with the paper.
gene2entrez <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Mm.eg.db, keys = unique(df_go$gene),
  keytype = "SYMBOL", columns = "ENTREZID"
)
df_go <- dplyr::left_join(df_go, gene2entrez, by = c("gene" = "SYMBOL"))
df_go <- df_go[!is.na(df_go$ENTREZID), , drop = FALSE]
df_go <- df_go[!duplicated(df_go$ENTREZID), , drop = FALSE]
ranks_dam_go <- df_go$stat
names(ranks_dam_go) <- df_go$ENTREZID
ranks_dam_go <- sort(ranks_dam_go[is.finite(ranks_dam_go)], decreasing = TRUE)

gsea_dam_go <- gseGO(
  geneList = ranks_dam_go,
  OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db,
  keyType = "ENTREZID", ont = "BP",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Original final plot excludes the GO descendants of translation and
# ribosome assembly before redundancy pruning.
translation_family <- unique(c("GO:0006412", GO.db::GOBPOFFSPRING[["GO:0006412"]]))
ribosome_family <- unique(c("GO:0042255", GO.db::GOBPOFFSPRING[["GO:0042255"]]))
drop_ids <- unique(c(translation_family, ribosome_family))
gsea_dam_go@result <- gsea_dam_go@result[
  !gsea_dam_go@result$ID %in% drop_ids, , drop = FALSE
]

# Retain original similarity and simplification settings.
gsea_dam_go <- enrichplot::pairwise_termsim(gsea_dam_go)
gsea_dam_go_slim <- clusterProfiler::simplify(
  gsea_dam_go, cutoff = 0.7, by = "p.adjust", select_fun = min
)
gsea_dam_go_slim <- clusterProfiler::setReadable(
  gsea_dam_go_slim, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID"
)
gsea_dam_go_df <- as.data.frame(gsea_dam_go_slim)

top_go_up <- gsea_dam_go_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(NES), NES > 0) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = NES, n = 7)

plot_df <- top_go_up %>%
  mutate(
    neglog10padj = -log10(p.adjust),
    Description = stringr::str_to_sentence(Description),
    Description = gsub("type ii", "type II", Description, ignore.case = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(NES) %>%
  mutate(Description = factor(Description, levels = Description))

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = NES, y = Description, fill = neglog10padj)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))) +
  labs(x = "NES", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", color = "black"))
```

### DAM1, DAM2, and combined DAM expression scores

The scores below are **mean log-normalized expression values**, not Seurat `AddModuleScore` values. Scores are computed per cell and then averaged by biological sample and condition.

```{r dam-module-scores}
# Keren-Shaul et al., Cell (2017), PMID: 28602351.
dam1_genes <- c("Tyrobp", "Ctsd", "Ctsb", "Apoe", "B2m", "Fth1", "Lyz2")
dam2_genes <- c("Trem2", "Axl", "Cst7", "Lpl", "Cd9", "Csf1", "Ccl6", "Itgax", "Clec7a", "Lilrb4a")
dam_combined_genes <- unique(c(dam1_genes, dam2_genes))

# The normalized expression layer should have been populated during the
# preceding microglia analysis; join layers as needed for Seurat v5.
DefaultAssay(dam_only) <- "RNA"
expr_mat <- GetAssayData(dam_only, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")

mean_signature <- function(genes) {
  present <- intersect(genes, rownames(expr_mat))
  if (!length(present)) stop("No genes found for signature")
  missing <- setdiff(genes, present)
  if (length(missing)) message("Missing signature genes: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  Matrix::colMeans(expr_mat[present, , drop = FALSE])
}

dam_only$DAM1_avgexp <- mean_signature(dam1_genes)
dam_only$DAM2_avgexp <- mean_signature(dam2_genes)
dam_only$DAM_combined_avgexp <- mean_signature(dam_combined_genes)

avg_scores <- dam_only@meta.data %>%
  group_by(sample, Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    DAM1score = mean(DAM1_avgexp, na.rm = TRUE),
    DAM2score = mean(DAM2_avgexp, na.rm = TRUE),
    DAM_combined_score = mean(DAM_combined_avgexp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(avg_scores)
```


```{r}

## DAM pseudobulk heatmap: AD versus AD-CXCL14
# Heatmap of DAM1 and DAM2 signature genes using normalized
# pseudobulk counts, log2 transformation, and row-wise Z-scores.
# Samples are ordered AD first, followed by AD-CXCL14.

library(pheatmap)

# DAM signatures (Keren-Shaul et al., 2017)
dam1_genes <- c(
  "Tyrobp", "Ctsd", "Ctsb", "Apoe", "B2m", "Fth1", "Lyz2"
)

dam2_genes <- c(
  "Trem2", "Axl", "Cst7", "Lpl", "Cd9",
  "Csf1", "Ccl6", "Itgax", "Clec7a", "Lilrb4a"
)

# Use the DAM pseudobulk DESeq2 object from the preceding analysis.
# This must correspond to AD vs AD-CXCL14 biological samples.
dds_heatmap <- dds_dam_go

# Select available DAM signature genes
dam_genes <- c(dam1_genes, dam2_genes)
dam_genes <- dam_genes[dam_genes %in% rownames(dds_heatmap)]

# Extract normalized pseudobulk expression
norm_counts <- DESeq2::counts(dds_heatmap, normalized = TRUE)
mat <- norm_counts[dam_genes, , drop = FALSE]

# Align sample metadata with the expression matrix
coldata <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(dds_heatmap))
coldata <- coldata[colnames(mat), , drop = FALSE]

# Explicitly set condition order
coldata$Condition <- factor(
  coldata$Condition,
  levels = c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
)

# Confirm that all samples belong to the two expected conditions
stopifnot(!anyNA(coldata$Condition))

# Order samples: AD first, then AD-CXCL14
ord <- order(coldata$Condition, coldata$sample)
mat <- mat[, ord, drop = FALSE]
coldata <- coldata[ord, , drop = FALSE]

# Column annotations
ann <- data.frame(Condition = coldata$Condition)
rownames(ann) <- colnames(mat)

ann_colors <- list(
  Condition = c(
    "AD" = "#F8766D",
    "AD-CXCL14" = "#00BFC4"
  )
)

# Generate heatmap
pheatmap::pheatmap(
  log2(mat + 1),
  annotation_col = ann,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  scale = "row",
  gaps_col = sum(ann$Condition == "AD"),
  show_rownames = TRUE,
  show_colnames = TRUE,
  fontsize_row = 18,
  fontsize_col = 10,
  border_color = NA,
  main = "DAM signature expression in AD and AD-CXCL14 microglia"
)

```


```{r}

## Percentage of DAM cells expressing selected DAM-associated genes
# Compare AD and AD-CXCL14 microglia.
# Each point represents an individual biological sample.

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(Seurat)

# 1. Select DAM cells from AD and AD-CXCL14 mice
dam_ad <- subset(
  dam_only,
  subset = Condition %in% c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
)

# 2. Define DAM-associated marker genes
dam1_genes <- c(
  "Tyrobp", "Ctsd", "Ctsb", "Apoe", "B2m", "Fth1", "Lyz2"
)

dam2_genes <- c(
  "Trem2", "Axl", "Cst7", "Lpl", "Cd9",
  "Csf1", "Ccl6", "Itgax", "Clec7a", "Lilrb4a"
)

genes <- c(dam1_genes, dam2_genes, "Spp1")

# 3. Extract log-normalized expression
expr_mat <- GetAssayData(dam_ad, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")

# Retain genes present in the dataset
available_genes <- genes[genes %in% rownames(expr_mat)]
missing_genes <- setdiff(genes, available_genes)

if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {
  message("Genes not found: ", paste(missing_genes, collapse = ", "))
}

# 4. Calculate percent-positive cells per biological sample
# Original criterion: log-normalized expression > 1
threshold <- 1

frac_by_gene <- lapply(available_genes, function(g) {

  gene_positive <- expr_mat[g, ] > threshold

  cell_data <- dam_ad@meta.data %>%
    mutate(gene_positive = as.logical(
      gene_positive[rownames(dam_ad@meta.data)]
    ))

  cell_data %>%
    group_by(sample, Condition) %>%
    summarise(
      gene = g,
      percent_positive = mean(gene_positive) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    )

}) %>%
  bind_rows()

# 5. Calculate mean percent-positive cells by condition
avg_frac <- frac_by_gene %>%
  group_by(gene, Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_percent = mean(percent_positive),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 6. Set plotting order
frac_by_gene$gene <- factor(
  frac_by_gene$gene,
  levels = available_genes
)

avg_frac$gene <- factor(
  avg_frac$gene,
  levels = available_genes
)

frac_by_gene$Condition <- factor(
  frac_by_gene$Condition,
  levels = c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
)

avg_frac$Condition <- factor(
  avg_frac$Condition,
  levels = c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
)

# 7. Plot percentage-positive DAM cells
ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = avg_frac,
    aes(x = gene, y = mean_percent, fill = Condition),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = frac_by_gene,
    aes(
      x = gene,
      y = percent_positive,
      color = Condition,
      group = Condition
    ),
    position = position_jitterdodge(
      jitter.width = 0.2,
      dodge.width = 0.8,
      seed = 1234
    ),
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    name = "DAM cells expressing gene (%)"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Gene",
    fill = "Condition",
    color = "Condition"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

## WT versus WT-CXCL14 microglia: pseudobulk DESeq2 and Reactome GSEA


```{r wt-microglia-pseudobulk}
library(Seurat)
library(DESeq2)
library(dplyr)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(ReactomePA)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# 1. Select WT and WT-CXCL14 microglia (all retained microglial states).
wt_micro <- subset(micro_sub, subset = Condition %in% c("WT", "WT-CXCL14"))
stopifnot(all(c("sample", "Condition") %in% colnames(wt_micro[[]])))

# 2. Confirm one condition per biological sample.
sample_info <- unique(wt_micro[[]][, c("sample", "Condition")])
if (anyDuplicated(sample_info$sample)) {
  stop("One or more sample IDs map to multiple conditions.")
}
stopifnot(all(sample_info$Condition %in% c("WT", "WT-CXCL14")))

# 3. Sum raw RNA counts per sample; do not aggregate by condition.
# AggregateExpression uses the raw RNA counts by default.
wt_counts <- AggregateExpression(
  wt_micro,
  assays = "RNA",
  group.by = "sample",
  return.seurat = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)$RNA

# 4. Align metadata by explicit sample names (no parsing of column names).
wt_coldata <- sample_info[match(colnames(wt_counts), sample_info$sample), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(wt_coldata) <- wt_coldata$sample
stopifnot(!anyNA(wt_coldata$sample), identical(rownames(wt_coldata), colnames(wt_counts)))
wt_coldata$Condition <- factor(wt_coldata$Condition, levels = c("WT", "WT-CXCL14"))
print(table(wt_coldata$Condition))

# 5. Fit a dedicated DESeq2 model for this comparison.
# REVIEW: confirm the count-filtering threshold used for the final figure.
wt_counts <- wt_counts[rowSums(wt_counts) >= 10, , drop = FALSE]
dds_wt_microglia <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(as.matrix(wt_counts)),
  colData = wt_coldata,
  design = ~ Condition
)
dds_wt_microglia <- DESeq(dds_wt_microglia)
res_WTcx_WT <- results(
  dds_wt_microglia,
  contrast = c("Condition", "WT-CXCL14", "WT")
)
summary(res_WTcx_WT)
```

```{r wt-microglia-reactome}
# 6. Map mouse SYMBOL identifiers to ENTREZ IDs and rank by DESeq2 Wald statistic.
res4 <- as.data.frame(res_WTcx_WT)
res4 <- res4[!is.na(res4$stat), , drop = FALSE]
res4$gene <- rownames(res4)

gene2entrez_list4 <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Mm.eg.db,
  keys = unique(res4$gene),
  keytype = "SYMBOL",
  columns = "ENTREZID"
)

df_list4 <- dplyr::left_join(res4, gene2entrez_list4,
                             by = c("gene" = "SYMBOL"))
df_list4 <- df_list4[!is.na(df_list4$ENTREZID), , drop = FALSE]
# Preserve the original analysis's first-occurrence rule for duplicate IDs.
df_list4 <- df_list4[!duplicated(df_list4$ENTREZID), , drop = FALSE]

ranks_list4 <- df_list4$stat
names(ranks_list4) <- df_list4$ENTREZID
ranks_list4 <- sort(ranks_list4[is.finite(ranks_list4)], decreasing = TRUE)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(names(ranks_list4)))

# 7. Reactome GSEA.
gsea_reactome_list4 <- ReactomePA::gsePathway(
  geneList = ranks_list4,
  organism = "mouse",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  verbose = FALSE
)

gsea_reactome_list4_df <- as.data.frame(gsea_reactome_list4) %>%
  group_by(Description) %>%
  slice_min(order_by = p.adjust, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

# Exclude translation/ribosomal pathway descriptions, as in the original code.
gsea_reactome_list4_df <- gsea_reactome_list4_df %>%
  filter(!grepl("40S|43S|ternary|translation|ribosom|rRNA",
                Description, ignore.case = TRUE))

# 8. Remove highly overlapping pathways by leading-edge Jaccard similarity.
# Preserve the original >0.4 cutoff and p.adjust preference.
gsea_reactome_list4_df$core_genes_entrez <- strsplit(
  as.character(gsea_reactome_list4_df$core_enrichment), "/"
)

jaccard <- function(a, b) {
  union_genes <- union(a, b)
  if (length(union_genes) == 0) return(0)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union_genes)
}

sets <- gsea_reactome_list4_df$core_genes_entrez
keep_pathway <- rep(TRUE, length(sets))

for (i in seq_along(sets)) {
  if (!keep_pathway[i]) next
  for (j in seq_along(sets)) {
    if (i < j && keep_pathway[j] && jaccard(sets[[i]], sets[[j]]) > 0.4) {
      if (gsea_reactome_list4_df$p.adjust[i] <= gsea_reactome_list4_df$p.adjust[j]) {
        keep_pathway[j] <- FALSE
      } else {
        keep_pathway[i] <- FALSE
      }
    }
  }
}

gsea_reactome_list4_df_filtered <- gsea_reactome_list4_df[keep_pathway, , drop = FALSE]

# 9. Annotate leading-edge genes with symbols.
all_entrez <- unique(unlist(strsplit(
  as.character(gsea_reactome_list4_df_filtered$core_enrichment), "/"
)))
entrez2symbol <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
  org.Mm.eg.db,
  keys = all_entrez,
  keytype = "ENTREZID",
  column = "SYMBOL",
  multiVals = "first"
)

gsea_reactome_list4_df_filtered$leading_edge_symbols <- vapply(
  gsea_reactome_list4_df_filtered$core_enrichment,
  function(x) {
    syms <- entrez2symbol[strsplit(x, "/")[[1]]]
    paste(stats::na.omit(syms), collapse = ", ")
  },
  character(1)
)
```

```{r wt-microglia-reactome-plot}
# 10. Plot top 10 positively enriched Reactome pathways.
# These are selected by NES
top_reactome_up <- gsea_reactome_list4_df_filtered %>%
  filter(!is.na(NES), NES > 0) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = NES, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)

plot_df <- top_reactome_up %>%
  mutate(
    neglog10padj = -log10(p.adjust),
    Description = stringr::str_to_sentence(Description),
    Description = gsub("nmda", "NMDA", Description, ignore.case = TRUE),
    Description = gsub("igfbps", "IGFBPs", Description, ignore.case = TRUE),
    Description = gsub("igf", "IGF", Description, ignore.case = TRUE),
    Description = gsub("hs-gag", "HS-GAG", Description, ignore.case = TRUE),
    Description = gsub("ca\\+\\+", "Ca²⁺", Description, perl = TRUE),
    Description = gsub(
      "Regulation of insulin-like growth factor \\(IGF\\) transport and uptake by insulin-like growth factor binding proteins \\(IGFBPs\\)",
      "Regulation of IGF transport and uptake by IGFBPs",
      Description
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(NES) %>%
  mutate(Description = factor(Description, levels = Description))

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = NES, y = Description, fill = neglog10padj)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "viridis",
    name = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value"))
  ) +
  labs(x = "NES", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", color = "black"))
```



## IFN microglia: AD-CXCL14 versus AD pseudobulk and GO enrichment

This section analyzes interferon-response microglia from AD and AD-CXCL14 animals.
Counts are aggregated at the biological-sample level before DESeq2. GO Biological
Process enrichment uses Wald statistics ranked by Entrez gene ID. Pathways are
simplified by GO semantic similarity and then by leading-edge gene overlap.

```{r ifn-pseudobulk}
library(Seurat)
library(DESeq2)
library(dplyr)
library(Matrix)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

# Retain only IFN-response microglia from the two AD genotypes.
micro_ifn_ad <- subset(
  micro_sub,
  subset = micro_subtype == "Interferon" &
    Condition %in% c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
)
DefaultAssay(micro_ifn_ad) <- "RNA"

# This analysis uses raw, unnormalized RNA counts (not Harmony embeddings).
# Join sample-specific Seurat v5 layers when necessary.
if (inherits(micro_ifn_ad[["RNA"]], "Assay5")) {
  micro_ifn_ad <- JoinLayers(micro_ifn_ad, assay = "RNA")
}
counts_ifn <- Seurat::GetAssayData(micro_ifn_ad, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
meta_ifn <- micro_ifn_ad[[]]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(counts_ifn), rownames(meta_ifn)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(meta_ifn$sample), !anyNA(meta_ifn$Condition))

# Validate one genotype assignment for each biological sample.
sample_meta_ifn <- unique(meta_ifn[, c("sample", "Condition")])
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sample_meta_ifn$sample))
print(table(sample_meta_ifn$Condition))

# Pseudobulk sum by sample. Avoid converting the full sparse matrix to dense.
cell_indices <- split(seq_len(ncol(counts_ifn)), meta_ifn$sample)
pb_ifn <- do.call(cbind, lapply(cell_indices, function(idx) {
  Matrix::rowSums(counts_ifn[, idx, drop = FALSE])
}))
colnames(pb_ifn) <- names(cell_indices)

coldata_ifn <- sample_meta_ifn[
  match(colnames(pb_ifn), sample_meta_ifn$sample), , drop = FALSE
]
rownames(coldata_ifn) <- coldata_ifn$sample
stopifnot(identical(colnames(pb_ifn), rownames(coldata_ifn)))
coldata_ifn$Condition <- factor(
  coldata_ifn$Condition, levels = c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
)
stopifnot(all(table(coldata_ifn$Condition) >= 2))

# Preserve the original filtering rule: >=10 counts in >=3 samples.
dds_ifn <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(pb_ifn),
  colData = coldata_ifn,
  design = ~ Condition
)
keep_ifn <- rowSums(DESeq2::counts(dds_ifn) >= 10) >= 3
dds_ifn <- dds_ifn[keep_ifn, ]
dds_ifn <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds_ifn)
res_ifn <- DESeq2::results(
  dds_ifn, contrast = c("Condition", "AD-CXCL14", "AD")
)
res_ifn_df <- as.data.frame(res_ifn)
res_ifn_df$gene <- rownames(res_ifn_df)
summary(res_ifn)
```

## GO Biological Process GSEA

```{r ifn-go-gsea}
# Original input gene identifiers were mouse gene symbols.
res_ifn_clean <- res_ifn_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(stat), is.finite(stat))

# Map symbols to Entrez IDs; retain one entry per Entrez identifier.

gene_map_ifn <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Mm.eg.db,
  keys = unique(res_ifn_clean$gene),
  keytype = "SYMBOL",
  columns = "ENTREZID"
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ENTREZID)) %>%
  distinct(SYMBOL, ENTREZID)

res_ifn_mapped <- res_ifn_clean %>%
  inner_join(gene_map_ifn, by = c("gene" = "SYMBOL")) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(stat)), gene) %>%
  distinct(ENTREZID, .keep_all = TRUE)

ranked_stats_ifn <- res_ifn_mapped$stat
names(ranked_stats_ifn) <- res_ifn_mapped$ENTREZID
ranked_stats_ifn <- sort(ranked_stats_ifn, decreasing = TRUE)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(names(ranked_stats_ifn)))

set.seed(1)
ego_bp_ifn <- clusterProfiler::gseGO(
  geneList = ranked_stats_ifn,
  OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db,
  ont = "BP",
  keyType = "ENTREZID",
  minGSSize = 10,
  maxGSSize = 500,
  pvalueCutoff = 1
)

# Optional annotated leading-edge table for inspecting the results.
gsea_ifn_results <- as.data.frame(ego_bp_ifn)
if (nrow(gsea_ifn_results) > 0) {
  core_ifn_long <- gsea_ifn_results %>%
    filter(!is.na(core_enrichment), nzchar(core_enrichment)) %>%
    mutate(ENTREZID = strsplit(core_enrichment, "/")) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(ENTREZID)

  entrez_symbol_map <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
    org.Mm.eg.db,
    keys = unique(core_ifn_long$ENTREZID),
    column = "SYMBOL",
    keytype = "ENTREZID",
    multiVals = "first"
  )
  core_ifn_summary <- core_ifn_long %>%
    mutate(SYMBOL = unname(entrez_symbol_map[ENTREZID])) %>%
    group_by(ID, Description, NES, p.adjust, qvalue) %>%
    summarise(
      core_genes_SYMBOL = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(SYMBOL))), collapse = ", "),
      core_genes_ENTREZ = paste(sort(unique(ENTREZID)), collapse = ", "),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  print(head(core_ifn_summary, 10))
}

# Remove redundant GO terms using Wang semantic similarity.
ego_bp_ifn_simpl <- clusterProfiler::simplify(
  ego_bp_ifn,
  cutoff = 0.7,
  by = "p.adjust",
  select_fun = min,
  measure = "Wang"
)
res_ifn_simpl <- as.data.frame(ego_bp_ifn_simpl)
```

## Prune overlapping pathways and plot enriched biological processes

```{r ifn-go-pathway-plots}
# Original selection: 50 largest positive NES and 50 smallest negative NES.
res_ifn_up50 <- res_ifn_simpl %>%
  filter(!is.na(NES), NES > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(NES)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 50)
res_ifn_down50 <- res_ifn_simpl %>%
  filter(!is.na(NES), NES < 0) %>%
  arrange(NES) %>%
  slice_head(n = 50)

jaccard_ifn <- function(a, b) {
  n_union <- length(union(a, b))
  if (n_union == 0) return(0)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / n_union
}

# Preserve original sequential pairwise pruning threshold (>0.5).
prune_by_jaccard_ifn <- function(df, cutoff = 0.5) {
  df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(core_enrichment))
  sets <- strsplit(as.character(df$core_enrichment), "/")
  keep <- rep(TRUE, length(sets))
  if (length(sets) < 2) return(df)
  for (i in seq_along(sets)) {
    if (!keep[i]) next
    for (j in seq_along(sets)) {
      if (i < j && keep[j] && jaccard_ifn(sets[[i]], sets[[j]]) > cutoff) {
        if (df$p.adjust[i] <= df$p.adjust[j]) {
          keep[j] <- FALSE
        } else {
          keep[i] <- FALSE
        }
      }
    }
  }
  df[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}

res_ifn_up_pruned <- prune_by_jaccard_ifn(res_ifn_up50, 0.5)
res_ifn_down_pruned <- prune_by_jaccard_ifn(res_ifn_down50, 0.5)

# Display names only; original p-values/NES are unchanged.
format_go_label_ifn <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_to_sentence(x)
  x <- gsub("type ii", "type II", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\\bb cell\\b", "B cell", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("^Erad", "ERAD", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("^Er-", "ER–", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("er nucleus", "ER–nucleus", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("^Dna", "DNA", x)
  x <- gsub("Interferon-alpha", "Interferon-α", x)
  x
}

# Upregulated: top 10 by largest positive NES.
plot_ifn_up <- res_ifn_up_pruned %>%
  filter(!is.na(NES), NES > 0) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = NES, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    neglog10p = -log10(pvalue),
    Description = format_go_label_ifn(Description)
  ) %>%
  arrange(NES) %>%
  mutate(Description = factor(Description, levels = Description))

p_ifn_go_up <- ggplot(plot_ifn_up, aes(x = NES, y = Description, fill = neglog10p)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = expression(-log[10]("p-value"))) +
  labs(x = "NES", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )
print(p_ifn_go_up)

# Downregulated: top 10 by most negative NES.
plot_ifn_down <- res_ifn_down_pruned %>%
  filter(!is.na(NES), NES < 0) %>%
  slice_min(order_by = NES, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    neglog10p = -log10(pvalue),
    Description = format_go_label_ifn(Description)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(NES)) %>%
  mutate(Description = factor(Description, levels = Description))

p_ifn_go_down <- ggplot(plot_ifn_down, aes(x = NES, y = Description, fill = neglog10p)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", name = expression(-log[10]("p-value"))) +
  labs(x = "NES", y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", color = "black"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )
print(p_ifn_go_down)
```


## IFN-response microglia: signature heatmap and expression scores

The following analyses use a 13-gene type I interferon (IFN) signature. The heatmap shows mean expression per biological sample among IFN-response microglia from AD and AD-CXCL14 mice. The expression score is the per-cell mean of log-normalized expression across the same genes, subsequently averaged by biological sample. This is not Seurat's `AddModuleScore()` method.

```{r ifn-signature-setup}
# Packages used in this section
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(Matrix)
library(pheatmap)

# Gene signature used in both analyses
ifn_genes <- c(
  "Stat1", "Stat2", "Irf7",
  "Mx1", "Isg15", "Ifit1", "Ifit3", "Oasl2",
  "Ifi203", "Ifi204", "Ifi205", "Ifi207", "Ifi209"
)

# Restrict to IFN-response microglia in the two AD conditions
micro_ifn_ad <- subset(
  micro_sub,
  subset = micro_subtype == "Interferon" &
    Condition %in% c("AD", "AD-CXCL14")
)
DefaultAssay(micro_ifn_ad) <- "RNA"

# The RNA data layer is expected to contain log-normalized expression.
# JoinLayers is included only if this assay has split layers; inspect the
# Seurat assay structure if this operation differs from the original pipeline.
# micro_ifn_ad <- JoinLayers(micro_ifn_ad, assay = "RNA")

rna_ifn <- GetAssayData(micro_ifn_ad, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")
available_ifn_genes <- ifn_genes[ifn_genes %in% rownames(rna_ifn)]
missing_ifn_genes <- setdiff(ifn_genes, available_ifn_genes)
if (length(missing_ifn_genes)) {
  message("Missing IFN genes: ", paste(missing_ifn_genes, collapse = ", "))
}
if (!length(available_ifn_genes)) stop("No IFN signature genes found")

# Confirm one biological condition per sample
sample_key <- micro_ifn_ad@meta.data %>%
  distinct(sample, Condition) %>%
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sample_key$sample), !anyNA(sample_key$Condition))
sample_key$Condition <- factor(sample_key$Condition,
                               levels = c("AD", "AD-CXCL14"))
sample_key <- sample_key[order(sample_key$Condition, sample_key$sample), , drop = FALSE]
print(sample_key)
```

### IFN signature heatmap

The heatmap uses Seurat's `AverageExpression()` on the RNA log-normalized data layer, then applies row-wise Z-score scaling. Samples are displayed AD first and AD-CXCL14 second without row or column clustering.

```{r ifn-signature-heatmap}
avg_ifn_sample <- AverageExpression(
  micro_ifn_ad,
  group.by = "sample",
  features = available_ifn_genes,
  assays = "RNA",
  layer = "data",
  verbose = FALSE
)$RNA

# Seurat can prefix sample identifiers beginning with digits with "g".
# Resolve both possible forms without assuming how a particular version behaves.
expected_samples <- as.character(sample_key$sample)
resolve_col <- function(sid) {
  candidates <- c(sid, paste0("g", sid))
  matches <- intersect(candidates, colnames(avg_ifn_sample))
  if (length(matches) != 1L) {
    stop("Cannot uniquely match sample ", sid, " to AverageExpression columns")
  }
  matches
}
avg_columns <- vapply(expected_samples, resolve_col, character(1))

mat_ifn <- as.matrix(avg_ifn_sample[
  available_ifn_genes, avg_columns, drop = FALSE
])
colnames(mat_ifn) <- expected_samples

#  removed genes with zero variance / invalid values.
valid_rows <- apply(mat_ifn, 1, function(x) {
  all(is.finite(x)) && is.finite(stats::sd(x)) && stats::sd(x) > 0
})
mat_ifn <- mat_ifn[valid_rows, , drop = FALSE]
if (!nrow(mat_ifn)) stop("No variable IFN genes remain for heatmap")

annotation_ifn <- data.frame(Condition = sample_key$Condition)
rownames(annotation_ifn) <- expected_samples
stopifnot(identical(rownames(annotation_ifn), colnames(mat_ifn)))

ann_colors_ifn <- list(
  Condition = c("AD" = "#F8766D", "AD-CXCL14" = "#00BFC4")
)

pheatmap::pheatmap(
  mat_ifn,
  scale = "row",
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  gaps_col = sum(annotation_ifn$Condition == "AD"),
  annotation_col = annotation_ifn,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors_ifn,
  fontsize_row = 18,
  fontsize_col = 10,
  angle_col = 45,
  border_color = NA,
  main = "Type I IFN signature (microglia)"
)
```

### IFN expression score by biological sample

For each cell, calculate the mean log-normalized expression of the detected IFN signature genes, then take the mean across IFN-response microglia from each mouse. .

```{r ifn-signature-score}
# Use the same selected IFN-response microglia and expression layer as above.
# Calculating on micro_sub before subsetting gives identical per-cell raw scores;

ifn_cell_scores <- Matrix::colMeans(
  rna_ifn[available_ifn_genes, , drop = FALSE]
)
micro_ifn_ad$IFNscore_raw <- ifn_cell_scores[colnames(micro_ifn_ad)]

# Optional within-subset Z-score; not used for sample means
micro_ifn_ad$IFNscore_z <- as.numeric(scale(micro_ifn_ad$IFNscore_raw))

sample_means <- micro_ifn_ad@meta.data %>%
  group_by(sample, Condition) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_IFN = mean(IFNscore_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cells = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = c("AD", "AD-CXCL14"))) %>%
  arrange(Condition, sample)

print(sample_means)

# Optional: show individual biological replicates 
ggplot(sample_means, aes(x = Condition, y = mean_IFN, color = Condition)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean IFN signature expression per sample") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

```


```{r}

## Microglial cell-state marker expression


library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Set the order of microglial subpopulations
state_order <- c(
  "Homeostatic",
  "Primed",
  "DAM",
  "Interferon",
  "Cycling"
)

micro_sub_dotplot <- micro_sub

micro_sub_dotplot$micro_subtype <- factor(
  micro_sub_dotplot$micro_subtype,
  levels = state_order
)

Idents(micro_sub_dotplot) <- "micro_subtype"

# 2. Define canonical marker genes for each state
microglia_markers <- list(
  Homeostatic = c("P2ry12", "Tmem119", "Cx3cr1"),
  Primed      = c("Arhgap15", "Ipcef1", "Oprm1"),
  DAM         = c("Tyrobp", "Trem2", "Apoe", "Ctsd", "Ctsb"),
  Interferon  = c("Mx1", "Ifit3", "Oasl2"),
  Cycling     = c("Mki67", "Top2a", "Birc5")
)

# 3. Prepare markers and their assigned gene groups
microglia_markers_vector <- unique(unlist(microglia_markers))

missing_genes <- setdiff(
  microglia_markers_vector,
  rownames(micro_sub_dotplot)
)

if (length(missing_genes) > 0) {
  message("Markers not found: ", paste(missing_genes, collapse = ", "))
}

microglia_markers_vector <- intersect(
  microglia_markers_vector,
  rownames(micro_sub_dotplot)
)

gene_groups <- stack(microglia_markers)
colnames(gene_groups) <- c("gene", "gene_set")

gene_groups$gene_set <- factor(
  gene_groups$gene_set,
  levels = state_order
)

# 4. Generate expression dot plot
p <- DotPlot(
  micro_sub_dotplot,
  features = microglia_markers_vector,
  group.by = "micro_subtype",
  assay = "RNA",
  dot.scale = 9,
  scale.by = "size"
)

# Associate each gene with its marker category
p$data$gene_set <- gene_groups$gene_set[
  match(as.character(p$data$features.plot), gene_groups$gene)
]

# 5. Final grouped plot
p_grouped <- p +
  facet_grid(
    cols = vars(gene_set),
    scales = "free_x",
    space = "free_x"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 12,
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

p_grouped

```
